correctness.rationale: Fourier diagonalization E_k=2J cos((2pi k+Phi)/N) yields the exact indexed two-energy difference 4J|sin((Phi+pi(j+k))/N) sin(pi(j-k)/N)|. For odd N, 2 invertible modulo N means independent sum/difference residues, giving the nearest-zero sine gap, uniquely maximized by quarter flux. For even N, equal parity of sum and difference gives min{sin(alpha)sin(alpha-theta),sin(2alpha)sin(theta)} in the reflected half-cell. Opposite strict monotonicities cross once at tan(theta*)=tan(alpha)/3; reflection yields exactly two maximizers and gap expression. Fourier Hilbert-Schmidt matrix units diagonalize the Cesaro dephasing difference with sinc factors; upper bound 2/(T Delta) is saturated at T=(2m+1)pi/Delta, establishing the claimed limsup and its parity asymptotics. Independent direct gaps across N=3..40 and 4560 flux comparisons matched; finite checks corroborate, not prove, all N.
residual_risks: Only nondegenerate flux has the rank-one Fourier dephasing as actual limit. The optimization is an asymptotic Hilbert–Schmidt limsup, not finite-time, trace-norm, diamond-norm, many-body or disordered-ring convergence.
